gap: No result ChatGPT got states that two European auto-club labs, ADAC (published 2025-06-11) and Switzerland's TCS, failed the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 that ChatGPT recommended for multi-day car camping. ADAC gave it 5.0 'mangelhaft' overall and in safety because its two DC inputs, the car input and the solar input, are not decoupled from each other. Charging from the car socket and solar at the same time can therefore push voltage into the vehicle's 12 V system and damage it.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rivals and the top result. OutdoorGearLab (2026-07-23) measured the Jackery 1000 v2 at 910 Wh usable, 85%, and the C1000 Gen 2 at 890 Wh, 87%. It gives no idle draw and no dB figures, does not review the RIVER 3 Plus, and says nothing about the DC-input defect. GearJunkie (2026-10-31) does not test the Explorer 1000 v2 at all. For the C1000 Gen 2 it gives only a 49-minute charge time, with no usable-capacity or idle measurement. Tested Watts (2026-09-23) says outright that it doesn't lab-test and uses only maker specs. I could not open Wired (fetch was blocked). I did not open the other nine results.
decides: ChatGPT's answer pitched the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 for 'multi-day car camping'. That is exactly the setup where someone tops up from the car socket and a solar panel together, and that is the setup ADAC and TCS flagged as able to damage the car's 12 V system. Two caveats: both labs tested the European unit, and I could not open a US Jackery page to confirm the US unit has the same two DC inputs. Given that, the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 is the safer car-camping pick. OutdoorGearLab measured it at 890 Wh usable and 87%, and it recharges in about 47–49 minutes. Its cost is a measured 13.8 W idle draw from The Solar Lab: by my arithmetic that is about 138 Wh, roughly 15% of the 890 Wh, if the inverter is left on overnight for 10 hours. If the Jackery stays on the page, it needs a 'never charge from car and solar at once' warning.

findings.label: ADAC test grade (overall and safety)
findings.note: ADAC downgraded it because the DC inputs are not decoupled. Test series published 2025-06-11, tested spring 2025, European model. It finished last with the Ective BlackBox 10.

findings.label: ADAC finding: car and solar DC inputs not decoupled
findings.value: If car and solar charge at the same time, voltage can pass from one input to the other and damage the vehicle's 12 V system (solar input up to 60 V / 400 W)
findings.source_title: Mobile Powerstations im ADAC Test: Nur die Hälfte schneidet gut ab
findings.note: Article dated 2025-06-11. ADAC notes the manufacturers did not explicitly rule out charging from both inputs at once. The EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus and Anker C800 Plus in the same test were not downgraded.

findings.label: TCS safety downgrade
findings.value: Score 0%, 'Abwertung aufgrund ungetrennter DC-Eingänge'; TCS says it would otherwise have placed 3rd
findings.note: Joint test with ADAC (June 2025). TCS notes parallel charging from vehicle and PV was not excluded in the manuals or on the device at the time of testing.

findings.label: OutdoorGearLab measured usable energy and efficiency
findings.value: 910 Wh of 1,070 Wh (85%); charging speed 563 Wh/hr; measured weight 24.4 lb
findings.note: By Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23. Test load not stated. The cited rival already has this figure. Ranked 7th of 14.

findings.label: The Solar Lab efficiency at near-max load
findings.value: 87.5% (37.5 min at 1,479 W vs 43 min expected)
findings.source_title: Jackery 1000 V2 Review: Has Jackery Learned from Their Mistake? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 1,479 W × 0.625 h ≈ 924 Wh delivered (my arithmetic). Measured AC recharge about 1 h 35 min in standard mode and just under 1 h in Emergency mode; solar recharge about 4.5 h at 400 W. No page date shown.

findings.label: The Solar Lab AC idle draw (inverter on, no load)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Review: Which Anker C1000 Version Should You Buy? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Over a 10-hour night that is about 138 Wh, or 15% of OGL's measured 890 Wh (my arithmetic). Same review measured about 86% efficiency (load not stated) and a 0–100% UltraFast AC charge in about 47 min. No page date shown.

findings.label: OutdoorGearLab measured usable energy and efficiency
findings.value: 890 Wh (87%); charging speed 1,097 Wh/hr; measured weight 25.2 lb
findings.source_title: The Best Power Stations of 2026 | Lab Tested & Ranked (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.note: Roundup updated 2026-07-23. The cited rival already has this figure. The page lists the rated capacity as both 1,024 Wh and 1,056 Wh. Text calls the fan loud near max output and not suited to overnight CPAP use; no dB figure.

findings.label: GearJunkie measured full charge
findings.source_title: The 11 Best Portable Power Stations | GearJunkie Tested
findings.note: Article dated 2026-10-31. Cited rival; no usable-capacity or idle figure.

findings.label: StorageReview discharge, recharge and UPS tests
findings.value: 0.43 kWh discharged; 0.56 kWh drawn from the wall to recharge; 9 ms UPS transfer
findings.source_title: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus Review: Compact Power Station with 600W Output, UPS Support (StorageReview)
findings.note: By Dylan Dougherty, 2025-02-12. Do not use as usable capacity: 430 Wh is about 50% above the 286 Wh rating, and the load and setup (possibly an expansion battery) are not stated. Only the 9 ms UPS figure is clean.

findings.label: ADAC: usable capacity versus rated, eight-unit test
findings.value: Usable capacity averaged about 10–15% below the maker's rated figure
findings.source_title: Mobile Powerstations im ADAC Test: Nur die Hälfte schneidet gut ab
findings.note: Eight ~1 kWh units tested in spring 2025 (Bluetti AC180P, EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus, Allpowers R1500, Anker C800 Plus, DJI Power 1000, Fossibot F1200, Ective BlackBox 10, Jackery 1000 v2).

unsourced: Whether the US Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (JE-1000D) has the same two DC inputs that ADAC/TCS faulted: a search snippet of Jackery's US FAQ said charging from solar and a car charger at the same time is 'Not supported' and gave separate car (12–16 V, 8 A) and solar (16–60 V) ratings. The FAQ page came back truncated in WebFetch and the jackery.com product page returned HTTP 429, so I could not open either.

A measured usable capacity or efficiency for the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus: OutdoorGearLab and GearJunkie don't test it, The Solar Lab's RIVER 3 Plus review gives no number, and StorageReview's 0.43 kWh is not credible for a 286 Wh unit. A CyberShack figure (226.8 Wh, 79%, Australian 240 V unit) appeared only in a search snippet and I did not open the page.

AC idle draw (inverter on, no load) for the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 and the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus: not given by The Solar Lab, OutdoorGearLab, ADAC, TCS or StorageReview; the only RIVER 3 Plus figures I saw were buyer anecdotes (9–18 W) in snippets.
Measured fan noise in dB for any of the three: OutdoorGearLab, The Solar Lab, TCS and StorageReview describe noise in words only; the '<30 dB' figures are maker specs.
Wired's 2026 roundup (rank 2): the fetch was blocked, so I could not check whether it reports any of these measurements.
